This isn't a scene from a film. This is a heartbreaking reality that still exists in parts of Nepal. For some women and girls, getting their period means being sent away from their own home to spend the night in a small shed, away from their families. They are left to face cold nights, fear, loneliness, and the danger of snakes, insects, and wild animals—all because of a natural biological process. Menstruation should never be a reason for exclusion or shame. Take a moment and ask yourself: If it were someone you love—your daughter, your sister, your wife, or your mother—would you accept this as "tradition"? Some customs deserve to be questioned, especially when they put lives and dignity at risk. Every woman deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued, no matter what day of the month it is. Let's raise awareness, start conversations, and stand together to end harmful practices like this. Wildest Festival Yet 🤯🐮 Only in Nepal will you find a festival to do with people passing away, cows, dancing, cross dressing and loads more.  Welcome to Gai Jatra - which literally translates to cow festival.  There’s a huge historical story behind it which is too long to explain here but essentially people originally took cows through the street as a way of saying  final goodbye to their loved ones but now for practicality they use these giant effigies call Tahamacha.  Hospitality of Nepal is off to a fantastic start absolutely loving it here but it feels like there is a festival everyday in Nepal - full video on this will be out on the Youchooobz at some point.  #nepaltiktok #nepal #kathmandu #gaijatra
